answer.rationale: The 18% mandate is binding and the low-cost vendor quote meets it alone; memory_c2 supports that vendor on cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy. But the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line runs at 94% with no buffer, so a wholesale cutover would raise delivery risk; a phased/guarded cutover (partial volume first, incumbent held as bridge) captures the mandate without creating the single point of failure memory_c3 warns against. Verifying c2 (does the low-cost vendor hold up under constrained/high-volume conditions?) and c3 (was second-source protection what actually preserved allocation?) before committing.
